newsitem.title: USA: Delta Air to code share with Transbrasil.
newsitem.headline: Delta Air to code share with Transbrasil.

text.p: Delta Air Lines and Transbrasil Airlines said on Wednesday they have signed an agreement that will allow the two carriers to provide code-sharing service between the United States and Brazil.

The agreement will strengthen Delta's international position by offering travelers in Brazil a chance to connect to more than 611 daily flights to 117 destinations, the companies said in a joint statement.
"Ninety-seven percent of U.S. bound Brazilian passengers can be served via Delta's Atlanta Worldport," Delta executive vice president of marketing Robert Coggin said in a statement.
The carriers said they are seeking approval from the U.S. Department of Transportation to operate code-share flights between several points in the United States and Brazil.
Pending government approvals, the carriers propose starting service October 12, 1997, the companies said.
The code sharing agreements will lead to enhanced reservation systems, schedule coordination between the carriers, sharing of facilities and mutual participation in frequent flyer programs.
